author: Allama Sayyid Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai (d. 1981 CE)
about: Twenty-volume Arabic commentary that explains the Quran by the Quran, followed by sections on narrations, philosophy and history. Volume and page numbers differ between the Beirut and Qom printings, so this platform cites it by verse.

author: Shaykh Abd Ali ibn Jumu'a al-Arusi al-Huwayzi (d. 1112 AH)
about: Collects narrations of the Prophet and the Imams under each verse, each attributed to its earlier source book.

author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi (3rd-4th century AH)
about: One of the earliest surviving Shia commentaries, transmitted largely from the narrations of the Imams. Scholars discuss the attribution of some later additions.

author: Muhammad ibn Mas'ud al-Ayyashi (3rd-4th century AH)
about: Early narration-based commentary. The surviving part covers the Quran up to Surah al-Kahf, and most chains of narration were shortened by a later copyist.

author: Amin al-Islam al-Fadl ibn al-Hasan al-Tabrisi (d. 548 AH)
about: Systematic commentary covering readings, language, grammar, meaning and occasions of revelation (asbab al-nuzul) for each passage.

author: Allama Muhammad Baqir al-Majlisi (d. 1110 AH)
about: Encyclopaedic collection of narrations (110 volumes in the Beirut edition) arranged by subject, with the author's explanations.

author: Thiqat al-Islam Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Kulayni (d. 329 AH)
about: Eight volumes: al-Usul (beliefs, volumes 1-2), al-Furu' (law, volumes 3-7) and al-Rawda (volume 8). Kitab al-Hujja in volume 1 holds most narrations on the Imamate and many verse explanations.

author: Compiled by al-Sharif al-Radi (d. 406 AH) from the words of Imam Ali (AS)
about: Sermon, letter and saying numbers differ between editions. This platform shows the numbering used by thaqalayn.net and links to each item.
